judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The img is the only content of a link to the news story 'Emoção e memórias marcam concessão de título de Professoras Eméritas às docentes Edna Oliveira e Janete Carvalho'; its alt, which becomes the link's name, describes the group photo. claimTrue: the snapshot shows the link holds only this img, and the alt says nothing of where the link leads. elementFails: an image that is the only content of a link is a functional image, and its text alternative has to identify what the link does (H30; WAI Images tutorial, functional images); this alt describes the photo instead, so a screen-reader user tabbing or listing links meets a picture description as the link. The headline link to the same URL that follows in the card is a separate link and does not give this one a purpose (H2 would combine them, or the image link would be removed from the tab order). captureDiffers: the live HTML fetched on 2026-11-21 has the same img, alt and href, and the screenshot shows the card as captured. The claim names this failure, so true positive.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The img is the animated GIF in slide 4 of an auto-playing slick carousel (autoplay, dots, variableWidth). claimTrue: in the snapshot its slide is not the current one and has aria-hidden=true, and no nearby text gives the emergency numbers. elementFails: yes, but not for the claim's reason. Slick removes aria-hidden from whichever slide is current, the carousel rotates every few seconds and its dots let a user pick this slide; the screenshot from the same run shows it as the current slide, when its alt is exposed. The image fails 1.1.1 because its alt is not equivalent: the GIF frames (checked on the live file) show Campus de Alegre as (28) 99901-9139 while the alt says 'Alegre: 27 99901-9139', and the alt leaves out the last frame (Polícia Rodoviária Estadual 198, Corpo de Bombeiros 193) and 'Central de Segurança'. The claim does not name that failure, so false positive. Visible non-current slides being aria-hidden (variableWidth) belongs rather under 1.3.1/4.1.2, and the auto-rotation under 2.2.2. captureDiffers: the live HTML has the same markup, alt and carousel settings; the aria-hidden state is one moment of the rotation that users also get.
